scenarios.hypothesis: A privileged browser-side consumer must reject a syntactically valid request when its synthetic origin/frame context, process instance, or routed-object generation does not match the authoritative ownership tuple.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use a controlled local browser fixture with synthetic origins, inert routed objects, and a read-only marker result so no real website, credential, or host-sensitive resource is touched.
scenarios.positive_control: The current synthetic origin, current frame/document generation, current renderer process generation, and current routed-object generation must resolve to the inert marker successfully.
scenarios.negative_control: Change only the synthetic origin or routed-object generation while keeping the IPC shape identical; the privileged side must reject the mismatched tuple and emit no marker result.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would require a real-user profile, third-party site, sandbox disabling, host privilege escalation, arbitrary code execution, persistent modification, or any non-inert effect.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, the previously accepted mismatched tuple is denied while the intended current-origin/current-process/current-object synthetic neighbor continues to return the inert marker.
scenarios.request_origin: The request originates from a deterministic synthetic page such as https://tenant-a.test with a fixture request identifier unique to this single controlled review case.
scenarios.browser_principal: The browser principal is the synthetic document/frame security principal reconstructed from browser-side state rather than a renderer-supplied string or unverified message field.
scenarios.origin_site_frame_context: Record the synthetic origin, site instance or equivalent browsing-context group, frame/document identity, and navigation generation used by the final browser-side policy decision.
scenarios.process_assignment: Record which renderer process instance the browser assigned to the synthetic site/frame and whether the assignment changed through navigation, process swap, reuse, or crash recovery.
scenarios.process_identity: Use deterministic fixture process identifiers for the current renderer and a neighboring renderer so process role cannot be confused with the exact process instance identity.
scenarios.process_generation: Assign explicit current and stale renderer generations; the stale generation represents a restarted or reused renderer slot and must never inherit the current generation's authority.
scenarios.sandbox_profile: Run under the release-equivalent local sandbox profile and record its fixture identity; debug-only or intentionally unsandboxed configurations are architecture notes, not proof.
scenarios.ipc_channel: Use one deterministic local IPC endpoint and message type whose sender process, receiver service, and interface version are recorded so the same channel can be replayed under paired contexts.
scenarios.message_state: Normalize the synthetic message into a stable operation, route identifier, object generation, and correlation tuple before routing; no hidden or real credential-bearing fields are required.
scenarios.routed_object_identity: Resolve the route/interface token to an inert fixture object with a unique semantic identity rather than treating the numeric route value itself as the security object.
scenarios.object_generation: Track the routed object's creation generation and a deliberately stale generation created by destroy-and-recreate in the local fixture so route reuse cannot masquerade as ownership.
scenarios.ownership_authorization_check: The privileged side must independently verify that the sending process/current frame principal owns or is authorized to reference the resolved current-generation object before use.
scenarios.broker_identity: The broker identity is a local mock browser-side service with a stable fixture identifier; it exposes no real host capability and only mediates access to inert synthetic resources.
scenarios.requested_capability_resource: The requested capability is read-only access to one inert marker resource whose canonical fixture identity is fixed; neighboring marker identities form the negative control.
scenarios.policy_decision: The policy decision must bind authoritative origin/site/frame context, sender process identity/generation, resolved object identity/generation, and requested marker resource into one allow-or-deny record.
scenarios.effective_brokered_authority: If allowed, effective authority is attenuated to read-only access for exactly the approved inert marker; no broader browser-service or host ambient authority is delegated.
scenarios.privileged_consumer: The privileged consumer is a mock browser-side handler that can only return the inert marker payload and decision receipt; it cannot perform arbitrary filesystem, device, network, or process actions.
scenarios.bounded_result: The only successful result is a deterministic read-only synthetic marker associated with the approved tuple; denied controls return an explicit denial and no side effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind each result to the fixture request correlation ID plus process generation, object generation, origin/frame identity, and capability/resource identity to exclude unrelated concurrent results.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: Advance frame/document and object generations during the fixture while keeping all old identifiers recorded; only the authoritative current generation may remain accepted after transition.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Replay the same normalized IPC request first with a neighboring synthetic origin and then with the stale object generation; each single-variable counterfactual must be denied independently.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude wrong-process attachment, expected site-process reuse, route-number recycling, stale telemetry, synthetic marker collision, delayed broker policy propagation, and unrelated concurrent receipt correlation.
scenarios.evidence_level: Target evidence level is B5 only if the bounded inert result is causally bound end-to-end and every required identity, generation, policy, counterfactual, and remediation condition is proven.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: The evidence ceiling remains below B4 when there is only route reachability, parser success, configuration review, or an unbound response; B5 additionally requires full causal provenance and regression proof.

scenarios.hypothesis: A valid IPC request from an authorized synthetic process must not inherit the mock privileged service's ambient authority or receive a broader capability/resource tuple than browser policy explicitly approves.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use a mock broker and inert capability sink in an owned local fixture; the oracle records only synthetic allow/deny decisions and canary receipts without invoking any real privileged host action.
scenarios.positive_control: A synthetic caller with the intended browser-side context requesting exactly the permitted inert resource receives only the narrow read-only capability and a matching deterministic receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: Keep caller identity and IPC syntax fixed but request a neighboring synthetic resource or wider operation; the mock broker must deny it rather than falling back to service ambient authority.
scenarios.stop_condition: Abort and do not proceed if the test would require real filesystem/device/network privilege, sandbox escape, production browser credentials, public extension behavior, persistent host change, or a target outside explicit ownership.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After the policy or broker binding is fixed, the over-broad synthetic request is denied while the narrow intended inert capability remains usable and produces the same correctly bound receipt.
scenarios.request_origin: The initiating request comes from a deterministic synthetic browser document with a unique fixture request ID and no external network dependency or third-party origin interaction.
scenarios.browser_principal: The browser principal is derived from authoritative local browser context for the synthetic document and is not accepted from an untrusted renderer-provided principal or origin field.
scenarios.origin_site_frame_context: Capture the authoritative synthetic origin, site/frame identity, document generation, and permission context that the browser uses when deciding whether the requested capability is permitted.
scenarios.process_assignment: Bind the synthetic document to one recorded renderer process assignment and keep a neighboring process available as a counterfactual without changing the process role or interface schema.
scenarios.process_identity: Use one exact caller renderer fixture identity and one neighboring renderer identity; the mock broker decision must reference the caller instance rather than the generic renderer role.
scenarios.process_generation: Record the caller renderer generation and reject an otherwise identical request from a stale generation so capability delegation cannot silently survive restart or process reuse.
scenarios.sandbox_profile: Use the local release-equivalent sandbox profile and record that the mock capability sink is intentionally inert; a debug-only or unsandboxed mode cannot raise the evidence level.
scenarios.ipc_channel: Send both positive and negative requests through the same deterministic IPC interface version and endpoint so capability-policy differences cannot be attributed to different transport paths.
scenarios.message_state: Normalize operation, resource, route/object identity, and request correlation fields before the broker decision; parser acceptance alone is recorded separately from authorization outcome.
scenarios.routed_object_identity: Resolve any interface or route token to the exact current synthetic broker object whose owner and lifecycle are known; numeric route reachability is never treated as capability authority.
scenarios.object_generation: The broker object carries an explicit generation that changes on fixture restart; requests referencing the old generation form a bounded lifecycle negative control.
scenarios.ownership_authorization_check: Verify that the caller process/context is authorized to reference the current broker object and then evaluate capability policy separately, preserving both decisions in the evidence record.
scenarios.broker_identity: The broker is a deterministic mock privileged service with broad simulated ambient privileges but an enforcement layer that may delegate only named inert capabilities to the caller.
scenarios.requested_capability_resource: The positive request asks for read-only access to marker-A while the counterfactual asks for marker-B or a wider synthetic operation, allowing exact requested-resource comparison.
scenarios.policy_decision: The policy record must include caller principal, process/generation, authoritative origin/frame context, requested operation/resource, broker object generation, and the explicitly approved capability tuple.
scenarios.effective_brokered_authority: Effective authority must equal or be narrower than the approved tuple: read-only marker-A access only, with no implicit access to marker-B or any simulated ambient broker privilege.
scenarios.privileged_consumer: The consumer is an inert mock capability service that can only emit a deterministic canary receipt for approved marker reads and has no path to real host-sensitive resources.
scenarios.bounded_result: A successful positive request returns one synthetic canary receipt naming marker-A and read-only operation; every wider or neighboring request returns denial without side effects.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Receipt fields bind request correlation ID, caller process/generation, browser principal, requested and effective capability, broker generation, and marker resource identity into one deterministic record.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: Restart the mock broker or advance its policy generation in the controlled fixture and confirm old delegated capability state is not reused after the authoritative generation changes.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold IPC bytes and caller constant while varying only the requested synthetic resource, then hold resource constant while varying only the caller process generation; both unauthorized variants must fail.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Eliminate parser-version drift, mock-broker restart races, stale policy cache, benign retry, wrong process correlation, synthetic marker collision, and result reuse from another request before promotion.
scenarios.evidence_level: B5 is reached only when the inert capability result proves requested-to-effective attenuation, authoritative caller/context binding, lifecycle control, counterfactual denial, and remediation regression end-to-end.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Without a bounded result tied to the exact approved capability tuple, evidence is capped below B4; broker reachability, valid IPC, or knowledge of service ambient privilege cannot establish B5.

scenarios.hypothesis: Browser restart, renderer process swap, routed-object reuse, service restart, or permission revocation must invalidate stale synthetic process/object authority while preserving only the current intended generation.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use controlled synthetic old/current process and object generations, a mock browser service, and an inert canary resource; all state transitions remain inside an owned deterministic fixture.
scenarios.positive_control: After the lifecycle transition, the current synthetic process generation and current routed-object generation must access the permitted inert canary through the normal policy path.
scenarios.negative_control: Replay the identical normalized request with the stale process generation or stale routed-object generation; the mock browser service must reject it and emit no canary receipt.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop if proving stale authority would require interacting with real browser sessions, preserving unauthorized host state, escalating privilege, executing arbitrary code, disabling sandboxing, or touching any third-party target.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: The fixed implementation rejects all stale-generation synthetic tuples after restart/revocation while the current-generation intended flow still succeeds with a fresh correctly correlated canary receipt.
scenarios.request_origin: A deterministic synthetic local document initiates both pre-transition and post-transition requests using fixture correlation IDs that reveal no real user or site information.
scenarios.browser_principal: The synthetic principal remains logically equivalent across the planned restart while process/object generations change, allowing lifecycle binding to be tested independently from identity membership changes.
scenarios.origin_site_frame_context: Record synthetic origin, site/frame identity, and document generation before and after the controlled lifecycle event so expected navigation or document replacement is not mistaken for a bug.
scenarios.process_assignment: Record the pre-transition renderer assignment and the post-transition renderer assignment, including whether the role is reused while the concrete process instance or generation changes.
scenarios.process_identity: Use explicit old and current renderer process fixture identities so a recycled process slot or identical renderer role cannot be mistaken for continuity of the original process principal.
scenarios.process_generation: Assign monotonic synthetic process generations before and after restart/process swap; only the current generation may participate in an authorized post-transition request.
scenarios.sandbox_profile: Keep the same release-equivalent local sandbox profile across the lifecycle transition so differences in acceptance cannot be explained by debug-only or intentionally unsandboxed configuration.
scenarios.ipc_channel: Use the same deterministic IPC schema and logical endpoint across lifecycle checks while recording the concrete connection generation so transport continuity is not confused with authority continuity.
scenarios.message_state: The normalized message keeps operation/resource constant and changes only lifecycle-bound identifiers such as process generation, object generation, or broker generation for paired comparison.
scenarios.routed_object_identity: Destroy and recreate an inert routed object with the same human-readable purpose but a new semantic identity/generation, preventing route-number reuse from being interpreted as continued ownership.
scenarios.object_generation: Record old and current object generations explicitly; a stale object reference after recreation must fail even if a numeric route/interface value is reused by the local fixture.
scenarios.ownership_authorization_check: The post-transition ownership decision must validate current sender process generation and current object generation against authoritative state before any broker policy is evaluated.
scenarios.broker_identity: Use a mock browser-side service whose instance/generation can be restarted deterministically; old connection or policy state must not silently authorize the new service generation.
scenarios.requested_capability_resource: Both stale and current requests target the same inert read-only canary resource, isolating generation validity as the only intended security-relevant variable.
scenarios.policy_decision: The policy record must reject stale process/object/broker generation tuples and allow the current tuple, while preserving the exact authoritative origin/context and requested resource identity.
scenarios.effective_brokered_authority: Only the current-generation tuple receives narrow read-only canary authority; stale generations receive no delegated authority even if the mock service retains broad simulated ambient capability.
scenarios.privileged_consumer: An inert mock consumer returns a canary receipt only for the current-generation approved request and cannot perform any real system operation or persistent host modification.
scenarios.bounded_result: The current request returns a deterministic canary receipt; stale-generation requests return explicit denial, making the lifecycle difference observable without exploitation or destructive proof.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind each canary or denial receipt to request ID, process identity/generation, object identity/generation, broker generation, origin/frame context, and requested resource for causal correlation.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: Advance renderer, routed-object, and mock-broker generations in a documented sequence and record revocation/policy generation so every stale/current acceptance decision has an authoritative epoch.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Replay one request with only stale process generation, one with only stale object generation, and one with only stale broker/policy generation while keeping all other fixture state constant.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude expected process swap, route reuse, reconnect semantics, stale telemetry, broker cache delay, benign retry, synchronization lag, wrong-process attachment, and unrelated receipt reuse.
scenarios.evidence_level: B5 requires the bounded canary result plus complete generation provenance, authoritative ownership/policy traces, independent stale-generation counterfactuals, alternative elimination, and remediation regression.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Observed reuse of a PID, route number, connection, or object label without a causally bound accepted result stays below B4; B5 requires proving stale authority across the exact lifecycle chain.
